subject: Agriculture
title: Drones in Agriculture
description: A fast breakdown of Drones in Agriculture for builders.

hook.text: A drone surveys 500 acres in 30 minutes and spots the crop stress a farmer standing on the ground can't see.

buildup.text: Agricultural drones carry multispectral cameras that detect plant health by measuring light reflection from leaves.

discovery.text: NDVI imagery from drones shows nitrogen deficiency, disease, and water stress weeks before symptoms are visible.

twist.text: In Japan and China, drones spray pesticides on rice paddies—reaching terrain too steep or wet for ground machines.

climax.text: Drone spraying uses 90% less water and applies pesticide only where needed—reducing chemical use dramatically.

punchline.text: Eyes in the sky find problems invisible from the ground. Farming just got aerial.

quiz.question: How do agricultural drones detect crop stress?
options: Multispectral cameras measuring light reflection to identify health issues
